status: PROVISIONAL PILOT, 2026-10-17: engineering defaults for one conservative development run on the Mac. Not the adopted experimental protocol: model, split, input and truncation policy, loss, threshold and validation use all remain pending adoption (D-106). Rationale: docs/pilot-20261017-mac.md.

data.label_source_note: Explicitly selected D-105 AI-assisted review of DW's 150 labels (data/labels/dw150-reviewed.jsonl): pending review; not independent coding; not joint adjudication. Report statements are derived from the prepared manifest's record kinds, not from this note.

input.notes: Student interaction type and topic read the last token of '[end of student prompt]'; the two AI axes read the final token. The response always receives a fixed reservation of response_cap plus its markers, so the student-side input (budget max_tokens minus that reservation) never depends on the current response. Labels, targets, notes, flags, review history and source records are never read.

lora.notes: dropout 0 because torch 2.14 activation checkpointing does not replay MPS dropout masks (verified on this Mac)

loss.notes: finetuning/multihead.py example_loss. ND and 'none of the four applies' are ordinary observed codes. The values above are checked against what the trainer implements.

schedule.notes: one unpadded interaction per forward pass; the gradient of an optimizer step is the mean of its interactions' losses; an epoch's last group may be smaller than 8

validation.purpose: Held-out students only to (1) exercise prediction and the unified evaluation on students unseen in training and (2) record per-epoch validation loss as a descriptive over/underfitting signal. Not used to choose hyperparameters, epochs, checkpoints, thresholds, input policy or models; no repeated tuning or model comparison. The final optimizer step is evaluated once. Results are development validation against pending-review researcher labels, not final RQ3 performance and not human reliability.

decode.notes: 0.5 is labels.PROVISIONAL_THRESHOLD, a plumbing default, not tuned. A multi-select axis takes every code at or above it, or its single highest code if none reaches it, so it is never empty; an exclusive negative selected with positives keeps whichever side has the higher top score.
